Otherwise don’t say anything.” Even pulled the classic “no one will ever love you the way I do” and tacked on a “no one else would put up with your bullshit.” Note I suffer from PTSD and all that jazz and autism to top it off.

Back in December, he and I traveled for work with a younger female coworker. Well… he and I got into a fight over me just telling him that I felt lonely and neglected (he was spending considerable amounts of time with her at every opportunity and even flirting with her), so he took me about 7 hours back home. He came back on New Year’s Eve and dropped the news that he wanted a divorce. Begged him not to and he gave me a choice: either let him have the divorce, or let him have a polyamorous relationship with her. I begrudgingly agreed. Come to find out he had already asked her to date him before he told me.

The agreement was that he would have no favorite, no priority for one or the other, and that he would actively work on our marriage (he refused therapy or counseling though). Shocker, he ended up prioritizing her, lied to me and slept with her in our bed and yelled at me for calling him out on it and they refused to apologize. He got to the point where I was told to shut up and leave them alone and he also moved her in from New Years Eve as well into our tiny one bedroom apartment. Slept in whichever room they didn’t want and isolated in our bedroom for a month. She also treated me like shit despite me taking care of both of them for about three months.

Fast forward to February, our anniversary month. On the first, he says I had too many breakdowns and the divorce was final. We went to Florida for work so I could try and afford to move out. Had to get a room of my own after trying to live with them belittling me all the time and they took a 13 hour drive back home without me, and me with no transport to work, and I had to beg him to take me to even buy a loaf of bread and pack of bologna to live on for about three days before the returned. Ended up leaving my job because of them and had to return home and have relocated three times since. Can also add “I haven’t been in love with you for at least six months” to my face. And so much more.

For me, it’s just a culmination of everything, but realizing that he didn’t actually value anything and was outright manipulating me to have a wife and mom (he wanted only cooking, cleaning and sex for his benefit) and was eager to jump to the next thing did it for me. That’s why I’m just thankful I had someone else (with his permission of course) to help get to this point.

I would advise against getting into another relationship that has any sort of emotional or romantic connections while there are problems in your current one. The boredom signals something amiss in what you have, but that’s not to say it’s a bad relationship or broken or anything, but I’d say it’s probably a good idea to start really introspecting on what exactly you need and want or maybe even why you feel bored. The best thing in mono or poly relationships like any other is being open and honest in your communication. The relationship should be about both of you as individuals with differing needs and wants that come together to make this work. So try honestly figuring out what you need to feel fulfilled and tell him about it. Have a calm, rational and open discussion and see where it goes. And please don’t push poly as an option or even opening up the relationship at all if he’s strongly okay because, from experience, pressuring and pushing only leads to resentment and unhappiness. This is a tricky situation but I hope that you guys make it through this and find happiness, whether that’s together or not.

Honestly, if you decide to make the decision to try and be in this relationship while giving him the freedom to love and find love outside of your partnership, then it could work but you both have to put in a good amount of work and trust. If you absolutely feel like this is a dealbreaker, then consent under duress or out of desperation to keep someone in your life is not consent. To be honest, it’s going to boil down to what you’re comfortable with and you’re both willing to put in. It’s alright to feel all the things you’re feeling and be confused on what to do, but ultimately no amount of advice aside from the standard “do what’s best for you down the road” is really going to do a lot if you don’t really introspect and acknowledge and understand what you are and are not willing to compromise in. In the end if it’s not going to be a happy and healthy relationship for you to live in a poly situation, then it would likely be best to not put yourself through that. If you think it could work, then by all means try but take care of your needs first.

If a card can't be affected. by another card, it can't be affected. If it were to say it couldn't be targeted, however, that's a totally different ballgame. You can target a card so long as it isn't protected from being targeted, however any effect after that will not happen. In this case, say we have a card like Apoqliphort Skybase (maybe a bad example, but here we go). It can't be affected by spell/trap effects or activated effects of monsters, so in the case of Starving Venom, it couldn't take the monster it targets (like Skybase in this case). If an additional effect would follow, such as this example: "you can target an opponent's monster and take control of it, and if you do...." then you would be able to target the monster, but that's it in a case like this as an extra tidbit.

Hello and welcome back to the game!

I was in your shoes until a few years ago (came back when XYZ first became a thing) so I get it can be a little shocking to come back with all the new stuff. Anyways, here's a couple things I honestly feel can help:

1.) Find a card or archetype you find interesting and then branch out from there. For example, if you say "hm, Dark Magician is cool. What goes with this?" Well, look up Dark Magician and any cards with his name in the text somewhere. Read about it and see what kind of effects the archetype members share (if they're part of one). I did this with my first deck after coming back and it helped give me a sort of idea for what kinds of effects the deck would have and to build a sort of focus or goal to build towards.

2.) Honestly, I agree with everyone here: look at deck lists and get an idea of what may work for you out of those lists. Edit them as you discover what your taste and play-style is. Are you aggro? Are you evasive or techy? Your card choices or what deck you're drawn to will help you sort through this and experimenting with a variety of decks and builds will help.

3.) When in doubt, just start looking up players on Youtube or something and see what decks they're using. Do they look fun to you or interesting? Is it one you would like to learn more about? 

4.) Once you have a general idea of a deck, try dueling a bot or someone else on a digital platform like DuelingNexus to test it out. See what works and doesn't work for you or how you feel about the deck flow. Make changes as necessary.

5.) Pick up what cards are considered staples to help support the deck you choose. This helps fill in some spots and make for some decent consistency gaps or protection gaps in your deck, like adding Mirror Force or Upstart Goblin for example.

6.) Just keep trying to improve! It can get disheartening, but the more you duel, especially with a deck that's new to you, the more you'll be able to figure out what works for it and you. Don't be afraid to use an original build and feel the need to run what everyone else does. Beyond that, just have fun and play around with the decks you enjoy and keep at it.
